subject: invariance of factor intercepts in 2nd order factor model

messages.author: 5bcc00bc48f15cdb
messages.subject: invariance of factor intercepts in 2nd order factor model
parts:
Dear lavaan-users,

I have a question concerning testing (partial) measurement invariance in a 2nd-order factor model. 

In short: Which "intercepts" are affected by group.equal=c("loadings","intercepts")?

In long: The model is specified like this: 

NRI <- '
# Faktoren erster Ordnung
PSH =~ m1_nri5 + m1_nri8 + m1_nri2
PSB =~ m1_nri3 + m1_nri9 + m1_nri6
COM =~ m1_nri1 + m1_nri12 + m1_nri14

CON =~ m1_nri16 + m1_nri13 + m1_nri18
CRI =~ m1_nri4 + m1_nri11 + m1_nri7
ANT =~ m1_nri17 + m1_nri10 + m1_nri15

# Faktoren zweiter Ordnung
SUP =~ PSH + PSB + COM
NEG =~ CON + CRI + ANT

ANT ~~ .01*ANT'

For a graph of the model please look at the appendix. 
And we have been testing successfully for (partial) measurement invariance with help of the lavTestScore() function for different models, which are nested within each other:

Model 1: configural invariance
Model 2: invariance of 1st order factor loadings
Model 3: invariance of 2nd order factor loadings
Model 4: invariance of item intercepts
Model 5: invariance of 1st order factor intercepts

We now find that there is absolutely no difference between Model 4 and 5 in different samples, which leads to the question if the specified model 5 in the correct way:

#Modell 1 (configural)
fit_NRI_mv_groups <- cfa(NRI, data=data_cfa_mv,group="inf")

#Modell 2 (loadings)
fit.equal.load2xmv <- cfa(NRI, data=data_cfa_mv,group="inf",group.equal="loadings",group.partial=c("SUP=~PSH","SUP=~PSB","SUP=~COM","NEG=~CON", "NEG=~CRI","NEG=~ANT"))
anova(fit_NRI_mv_groups,fit.equal.load2xmv)


#Modell 3 (all loadings)
fit.equal.load3xmv <- cfa(NRI, data=data_cfa_mv,group="inf",group.equal="loadings")
anova(fit_NRI_mv_groups,fit.equal.load2xmv,fit.equal.load3xmv)


#Modell 4: Item intercepts
fit.equal.inter4xmv <- cfa(NRI,data=data_cfa_mv,group="inf",group.equal=c("loadings","intercepts"),group.partial=c("SUP~1","NEG~1","PSH~1","PSB~1", "COM~1","CON~1","CRI~1","ANT~1"))


#Model 5: intercepts of items and factors
fit.equal.inter5xmv <- cfa(NRI, data=data_cfa_mv,group="inf",group.equal=c("loadings","intercepts"))

anova(fit_NRI_mv_groups,fit.equal.load2xmv,fit.equal.load3xmv,fit.equal.inter4xmv,fit.equal.inter5xmv )

Output:
Chi Square Difference Test

                     Df   AIC   BIC  Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)   
fit_NRI_mv_groups   258 42063 42675 582.31                                 
fit.equal.load2xmv  270 42057 42608 600.50    18.1854      12   0.110175   
fit.equal.load3xmv  274 42052 42583 603.83     3.3336       4   0.503630   
fit.equal.inter4xmv 284 42061 42540 632.13    28.2951      10   0.001619 **
fit.equal.inter5xmv 284 42061 42540 632.13     0.0000       0   1.000000   
---
Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1


There must be a mistake in the specification of Model 4 or 5 although we cannot seem to find it. I greatly appreciate any help on this!

Thank you!
Lea

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: invariance of factor intercepts in 2nd order factor model
parts:
Lea--
     (By the way, your email was extremely clear and informative.)
     Yves recently explained (probably not for the first time) that lavaan changes some specifications for the intercepts / means of factors under different conditions.  I believe you have crossed one of those boundaries moving across your five models, invoking different sets of defaults from one model to the next.  It is important to remember that you are using the cfa function and not the lavaan function.  The cfa function has a larger set of programmed default behaviors. You might try overcoming these by imposing equality through using the same labels for different groups,i.e.:
SUP~c(a,a)*1
     It appears to me that,inn going from Model 3 to Model 4, the cfa function actually relaxed 2 constraints (or estimated 2 new parameters) while it was imposing equivalence on the observed variable intercepts.  If this were not so, then the gain in DF from Model 3 to Model 4 would be the same as the gain in DF from Model 1 to Model 2.
--Ed Rigdon
